name: Keresdrakon
isnote: Recovered as the earliest-diverging tapejaromorph (Kellner et al. 2019) or as sister to Alanqa at the base of Azhdarchoidea (Pêgas et al. 2022).
sum: Toothless azhdarchoid from the Early Cretaceous ‘Pterosaur Graveyard’ of Paraná, Brazil, found with Caiuajara and the theropod Vespersaurus.
holotype: CP.V 2069 — Goio-Erê Formation (bonebed C), Cruzeiro do Oeste, Paraná.
material: Disarticulated 3D partial skeleton of a subadult: snout, quadrate, lower jaws, vertebrae, sternum, girdles and limb bones.
biology: Found in direct association with the tapejarid Caiuajara and the noasaurid theropod Vespersaurus, showing the three lived together around a desert lake.
author: Kellner et al. 2019
